title: Troy Aikman calls out 'embarrassing' UCLA attendance amid Bruins' CFP push - CBS Sports
description: One of just two undefeated teams remaining, the Bruins drew less than 25,000 to their last home game
body:
One of just two undefeated teams remaining, the Bruins drew less than 25,000 to their last home game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Shots of a half-empty Rose Bowl are growing tiresome this season for UCLA legend Troy Aikman.The Pro Football Hall of Famer and former Bruins All-American sounded off earlier this month about the lack of fan support for the unbeaten program and isn't sure how to fix the lack of buzz in Los Angeles. Despite No. 8 UCLA's rise during Bob Chesney's impressive first season, the Bruins can't seem to generate interest from their fanbase."Little embarrassing that we were 7-0 going into last week's game (against Nevada) and, they shoot it pretty low (on TV) so you can't really tell when you're watching the game, I'm told there was about 20 to 25,000 people at the game," Aikman said recently on 96.7 The Ticket. "So when you have a stadium at the Rose Bowl that holds over 100,000, 25,000, it may as well be empty as opposed to some other stadiums that maybe hold 40,000."We've got to get people going to games; we've got to get them excited about it. And then you say, 'Well, how do you get them excited? If 7-0 doesn't get them excited, what will?' I don't know the answer to that."
Despite losing quarterback Nico Iamaleava to a season-ending injury, the Bruins have continued to power ahead toward a Big Ten Championship appearance and College Football Playoff berth behind Ty Dieffenbach and Wayne Knight on offense along with one of the nation's top defensive units."I told our guys, 'Don't worry about watching this four-week drama series that's going to be this new show that they're going to put out there,'" Chesney said after Saturday's win at Minnesota on what to make of the selection committee's first rankings. "That's not what we're here for. No way slighted. No way honored. Just totally neutral on whatever they might say. We've got to win our football games, and we did that today."Chesney touched on the Bruins' attendance issues and lack of fan engagement two weeks ago.
"I don't really turn around and look behind and see what's really going on," Chesney said. "We all got to do a better job of getting a little bit more involved and make sure our guys in classes are talking about this with everybody, making sure they can connect a story and face to this team, not just what this team is but ultimately the people on it. We've done everything we could as far as the tickets, the travel plans and the free access. "Our administration's doing a great job; we've just got to make sure everybody just keeps talking about it all the time, especially on this campus."During UCLA's last home win against Nevada on Oct. 31, the Bruins posted a season-low attendance of 24,611. According to USA Today, FBS home game attendance on Halloween this season was 8.8% lower than those teams' 2025 home game averages.
Duke and Stanford are the only two other Power Four programs this season filling less than 50% of their seating capacity for home games.The Bruins host Illinois on Friday night at the Rose Bowl before traveling to Michigan on Nov. 21. The rivalry showdown with USC on Nov. 28 should draw a packed stadium, given its significant Big Ten and CFP implications.

title: The lifecycle of golf, 19-year-old Blades Brown wins, Jon Rahm returns to relevance and WTGL debut - CBS Sports
description: The Tuesday Tee Sheet is busier than usual, given a weekend in golf that made a few surprising headlines
body:
The Tuesday Tee Sheet is busier than usual, given a weekend in golf that made a few surprising headlines
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:34 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Blades Brown and Ben James shook hands on the 18th tee at El Cardonal at Diamante Sunday evening, all eyes shifted towards the future. Who would win this playoff between these two young budding stars? What could the next five years and beyond possibly have in store for both of them?As hypotheticals were pondered and expectations were placed, shoulders slumped elsewhere on the property carrying a different kind of weight on body and mind. Denny McCarthy had lost again. In a career that has now spanned 240 PGA Tour starts, the former Virginia Cavalier has traversed the highest level of professional golf for almost a decade without stepping into the winner's circle. His T6 finish on paper is enough to push him inside the top 75 of the FedEx Cup standings and secure himself a place on tour in 2027, but it could have been so much more.With five holes remaining, McCarthy, 33, was tied with a kid 14 years younger than him. McCarthy had more holes to play; at a resort golf course like El Cardonal, where the biggest defense is yourself, that means there are more birdies to make. He failed to get up-and-down for birdie on the first par 5 and then 3-putted for bogey on the next hole.
His chances were damaged but not yet destroyed. That is until the par-4 17th. In need of a miracle, McCarthy tossed up a prayer with his second shot right of the fairway. The answer he was looking for (and his golf ball) was never found on the other end. A double bogey ensued. Anguish and despair rolled onto his exterior.McCarthy has had a very successful PGA Tour career given what he has been afforded. He is not the biggest. He is not the strongest. He is not the most talented. He is often labeled one of the best putters in the world, but he has repeatedly said he wants to be known for more.FedEx Cup Fall gets a bad rap. It's football season, the golf courses are resort-style and fail to test the game's best, and the stars are back home kicking their feet up or writing the first draft of some statement they are about to release that no one ever asked to read. 
They wait with excitement (some, dread) for the start of the season in January, when they will play against their their peers. They will play for an exuberant amount of money and on golf courses like Riviera and Pebble Beach. Meaning will be attached to these tournaments given the history and the stakes, but not to the extent we witnessed this Sunday. At the least, it will be different.On Sunday, we watched as a long-time PGA Tour player attempted to fend off the next wave. In an era where the middle class is going extinct, and fans and executives want to usher in the next generation as soon as possible to create more stars and more dollar signs, McCarthy tried to delay the professional golf life cycle.In one sense, he did. McCarthy locked up playing privileges for next season and reset his clock -- achieving a moral victory that won't be celebrated for long. As the likes of Brown and James begin mapping out their futures, McCarthy continues to fight a multi-front war flanked by a changing professional landscape, a wave of hungry new arrivals and a clock that is already counting down again.
What's my age, again?Blades Brown won on the PGA Tour last Sunday. Dare I tell you the year he was born? 2007. Feeling old yet?! It is unbecoming of the 19-year-old to make us feel this way at the start of another long week before the holiday season, but to the victors go the spoils. Brown became the youngest player since 1931 to win on the PGA Tour with his victory over James on the second playoff hole Sunday evening, taking that mantle from Jordan Spieth.Starting the day seven strokes off James' pace, Brown carded a final-round 9-under 63 that included four birdies in his final six holes. It looked as if he would claim the trophy without the added drama as he knocked in a 6-foot birdie putt on the 72nd hole to get into the clubhouse one better than his playing partner Michael Kim, but James had other ideas with an eagle of his own on the last hole to tie Brown.
Despite only being 19, Brown has already amassed an incredible amount of experience. He started his season by holding the 54-hole lead at The American Express and played alongside Scottie Scheffler and Si Woo Kim in the final group. He then earned special temporary status on the PGA Tour and went on to earn his full-time PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour, where he was the youngest graduate in history.The win moves him up to No. 62 in the world, meaning a couple more good starts could elevate him inside the top 50 by year's end when an invitation to a certain major championship is mailed out. Return to relevanceOne door closes, and another one opens for Jon Rahm, this one leading him into the winner's circle for his first relevant win since the 2023 Masters. In Rahm's first tournament since leaving LIV Golf, the Spaniard sizzled at the Abu Dhabi Championship and emerged from a crowded leaderboard that included Hatton and McIlroy at Yas Links.
The win represents Rahm's sixth Rolex Series title (most all-time) and his 11th DP World Tour victory.In a stroke of absolute hilarity, Rahm now has a real chance to win the Race to Dubai. The victory moved him up to No. 11 in the season-long race, and should he win the DP World Tour Championship (which he has three prior times) with Eugenio Chacarra finishing worse than eighth place and McIlroy finishing worse than runner-up ... guess what? Rahm wins the whole damn thing!That is where attention shifts in the short term. In the long term, inquiring minds want to know whether the PGA Tour will extend a lifeline for Rahm and how that would affect the relationship between the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. The league will not make any decision until the LIV Golf bankruptcy process is final.
WTGL debutsThese boots were on the ground synthetic turf Sunday at the SoFi Center as the WTGL kicked off its inaugural season. LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler hit a historic ceremonial first putt before taking part in a champagne toast to officially get the league underway.From what I gathered, everyone within the TGL ecosystem is really excited about this opportunity for the women's game. The same talking point of this being a great chance to showcase personality and entertain a wider, younger audience is already getting beaten to death, but those soundbites should only persist.The level of care from the players to those running the operations is there. That cannot be denied. Ultimately, I wonder what that level is from the outside world, though, and if success for this first run might be as simple as producing a new personality or two that golf fans were previously unaware of.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Ranking Vikings quarterback options with Kirk Cousins as best fit in Minnesota - CBS Sports
description: After Carson Wentz exposed Minnesota's offensive problems on national television, the 6-2 Vikings must consider a
body:
After Carson Wentz exposed Minnesota's offensive problems on national television, the 6-2 Vikings must consider an aggressive move
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:23 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Minnesota Vikings are the rare 6-2 team in crisis. After a brutal 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota finds itself looking for a new quarterback on trade deadline day. Starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions, putting Minnesota's broken offense on display for everyone to see on national television.Murray has been one of the worst full-time starters in the NFL, and "full-time" is a stretch, considering he's missed two games and most of a third due to two different injuries. Minnesota is 28th is offensive points per game (17.4), and its 11 offensive touchdowns are tied with the Chargers for fewest in the league.Changing starting quarterbacks in the middle of the season is far from ideal, but so is the Vikings' current situation. Continuing to roll out this level of quarterback play would mean wasting a Super Bowl-caliber defense. What Minnesota does at the game's most important position will change the entire tenor of the trade deadline, and there are quite a few options.1. Kirk Cousins, Raiders
Who says you can't go home? (Or, at least, back to one of your homes?) Kirk Cousins spent 2019-23 with the Vikings, the final two years of which were under Kevin O'Connell. Cousins played high-level football, especially in 2023 before tearing his Achilles, under O'Connell, and he has been a pleasant surprise for the Raiders, keeping the seat warm for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza.
This would not be a perfect solution -- there are none of those at this point -- as Cousins is coming off a three-interception game and isn't the player he was when he was in Minnesota previously. His mobility has taken a huge hit; he's 38 years old, and the arm strength has waned, too. But this would be the best option in a pinch. Cousins knows how to feed his best players the ball, and the Vikings have a great "best player" in Justin Jefferson. His experience in the system would help on a tight turnaround.One big question would be why the Raiders would make this trade. Even with Mendoza waiting in the wings, Las Vegas has little reason to do this. It would force Mendoza to make his first career start on a short week of preparation against the Seahawks, one of the league's best defenses. Cousins has been an important part of Mendoza's development, too. Splitting that duo midseason doesn't make sense, and Cousins' presence would continue to pay dividends once Mendoza does eventually take over.2. Geno Smith, Jets
Another well-traveled veteran playing solidly in a placeholder role, Geno Smith would be the second-best option for Minnesota. Moreover, the Jets showed a willingness to make big trade-deadline sales before, having traded both Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams at the deadline last year for king's ransom. Trading Smith and getting back some solid trade compensation would add to their considerable war chest of 2027 picks, which currently includes three first-round selections.
Smith had a miserable 2025 with the Raiders but has been much better with the Jets, cutting down on the turnovers while still delivering on some of his trademark downfield aggression. His 16 completions for 20+ yards downfield are the fourth-most in the league this season. Downfield passing has been a disaster for Minnesota this season.One issue here could be the Jets not having a proven backup. The only other quarterback on the 53-man roster is rookie Cade Klubnik, and Will Levis is on the practice squad. Would the Jets want Murray, who is on a cheap one-year deal anyway? If not, it might be hard to make this move; playing nearly half the season with a middle-round rookie is a tough look, even if New York is well out of the playoff picture. It's important to have a viable offensive ecosystem, if only to evaluate your personnel and keep the team engaged.3. Daniel Jones, Colts
The Colts reportedly told Daniel Jones they will not trade him, but what if the Vikings came in willing to overpay? The Colts have already sold off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and could move other veterans (Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart) before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. Jones has endured a brutal season, but he's also had brutal surroundings, including one of the league's most underwhelming groups of pass catchers.
Jones spent time on the Vikings' practice squad in 2024, but this would be an underwhelming reunion. Jones has been a turnover machine and one of the worst starters in the NFL this year, even worse than Murray. He has not had a single game with more passing touchdowns than interceptions. Perhaps O'Connell sees something we don't, but it's hard to envision Jones providing any meaningful upgrade.

title: MLB rumors: A new Tarik Skubal suitor, the Mets' vision, plus what the Braves plan to do with Ronald Acuńa Jr. - CBS Sports
description: Here are your hot stove rumors as the GM meetings open on Tuesday, Nov. 10
body:
Here are your hot stove rumors as the GM meetings open on Tuesday, Nov. 10
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:42 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This is an important week on the baseball calendar. First and foremost, it is awards week. Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart were named the Rookies of the Year on Monday. The Managers of the Year will be announced Tuesday, Cy Youngs and Relievers of the Year will be announced Wednesday, and finally the MVPs will be announced Thursday.  Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas. The GM Meetings are not the Winter Meetings in terms of the sheer volume of rumors and transactions, but they do usually provide some news. There could be more than usual this year given the near certainty of a lockout on Dec. 1, which would also mean there are no Winter Meetings. This may be the only time everyone is in the same room this winter. The three weeks between now and Dec. 1 could be quite active.  We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.  With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Padres have expressed interest in Skubal  
Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.  Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?  
  Morejon prefers to stay in the bullpen  
Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.  We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cubs hope to add three startersAlthough they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who is still recovering from a neck injury, and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain.
Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop.
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Mets not interested in major overhaul  Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.  The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk."

                            
    
                                                
                    
      Braves will not move Acuña  
Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Red Sox won't commit to Story at short  
On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. title: Predicting 2027 MLB Rookie of the Year candidates: Josue De Paula, Kade Anderson, Jesús Made and more - CBS Sports
description: Who will follow in Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart's footsteps?
body:
Who will follow in Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart's footsteps?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle and Reds slugger Sal Stewart were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year on Monday night. McGonigle was the wire-to-wire leader for the award despite a stacked American League rookie class. In the National League, Stewart edged out Mets outfielder Carson Benge and Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt, both of whom had excellent rookie campaigns.  No award gets you excited about the future the way Rookie of the Year  does. It's a young player being recognized for his greatness, and great  young players are what sports hopes are built on. With that in mind,  here's a look ahead at the 2027 rookie class and, more importantly, who could be in the  running for the 2027 Rookie of the Year awards.
        
            
                2026 MLB Rookie of the Year: Tigers' Kevin McGonigle, Reds' Sal Stewart win BBWAA awards
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
  American League  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LHP Kade Anderson, MarinersAnderson made his debut in late August and gave the Mariners seven solid starts, though he remains rookie-eligible because he did not exceed the rookie limits of 50 innings or 45 days of service time. Anderson, the No. 3 pick in the 2025 Draft, is arguably the best pitching prospect in the game and is likely to have a rotation spot on Opening Day, which figures to boost his Rookie of the Year case. Add in a pitcher-friendly home ballpark, and Anderson is the super early favorite for the award. He had 167 strikeouts against only 22 walks in 129 innings between MLB and the minors in 2026.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    SS Franklin Arias, Red SoxOne of the best prospects in the minors, Arias nearly made his MLB debut in September, but the Red Sox opted against it. He authored a .323/.400/.557 line with 25 home runs between Double-A and Triple-A in 2026, including a .331/.388/.506 line in 42 games at Triple-A as a 20-year-old. Trevor Story is entering the final year of his contract and has been healthy and productive at the same time once in the last four years. Arias likely gives Boston a better chance to win right now and I would not be surprised to see them turn the shortstop reins over to the youngster early next season. Early as in April.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    OF Walker Jenkins, TwinsLike Anderson, Jenkins made his MLB debut in late August, yet his rookie eligibility remains intact going into 2027. He had a rough go of it in the majors, slashing .226/.293/.393 in 26 games with the Twins, though his contact rates and plate discipline were impressive. Jenkins will turn only 22 in February and he is not the first top prospect to have a rough 26 games to begin his big-league career, nor will he be the last. There might be more growing pains to come next season, but Minnesota figures to give Jenkins a long runway to work through them. His 2027 could look like Benge's 2026, meaning sluggish early and sensational late.  National League  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    OF Josue De Paula, DodgersIt was only 11 games (plus four pinch-hitting appearances in the postseason), but gosh, De Paula was so impressive during his big-league debut. He's a precocious hitter with tremendous strike zone knowledge (13 walks and five strikeouts), and also some serious hard-hit ability. The biggest obstacle standing between De Paula and next year's Rookie of the Year award is playing time. Shohei Ohtani is locked in at DH and Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker aren't going anywhere. The Dodgers will have to either trade or bench Teoscar Hernández to get De Paula into the lineup. It would be worth it. The Yordan Alvarez comps De Paula got in the minors don't seem so insane now.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    IF Jesús Made, Brewers The Brewers are the World Series champions and they also have arguably the best farm system in the game with the consensus No. 1 prospect in Made. Still only 19, Made performed admirably in a full season at Double-A this year, and he's currently playing very well against grown men in the Dominican Winter League. He figures to open next season in Triple-A, with a May or June promotion to Milwaukee in the cards. That could put Made at a disadvantage in the Rookie of the Year race. Either way, it's only a matter of time until the defending champions add the game's best prospect to their lineup, presumably at third base.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    C Ethan Salas, PadresAt 20 years and 121 days, Salas became the youngest catcher to ever appear in a postseason game in Game 2 of this year's Wild Card Series. He started three of San Diego's six postseason games after making his MLB debut in September, and it seems likely Salas will take over as their starting backstop next season. I think he's a longshot Rookie of the Year candidate simply because it's really hard to be a rookie catcher, and next year Salas will be the youngest regular catcher since Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez in 1991. Still, Salas is a special defender with promising offensive chops.    International candidatesSeveral prominent Japanese veterans will make their way to MLB via the posting system this offseason. We don't know where they will sign yet, but the rules say these players will be Rookie of the Year-eligible regardless of their age or years of experience in Japan, so we're going to include them here.  
        
            
                MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
3B Teruaki SatoWe ranked Sato as the best position player free agent on the market this offseason. Japan's reigning Triple Crown winner has tremendous left-handed power. We're talking legitimate 30-homer upside. Sato does swing and miss a bunch, though, and he's an aggressive hitter who's unlikely to walk as much as Munetaka Murakami, which could hold him back at the plate. Add in questionable defense at the hot corner and it's unclear exactly how much impact Sato will have in the big leagues. Bottom line though, guys with 30-homer power will always be in the Rookie of the Year conversation.  
RHP Kaima TairaTaira, our No. 19 free agent, is destined to be a fan favorite given his fire hydrant build (5-foot-8 and 220 lbs.) and bat-missing fastball. He gets close to seven feet of extension down the mound despite his height, creating a unique release window and an "upshoot" effect on his fastball. Taira started for the Seibu Lions in 2026 after spending 2024 and 2025 in the bullpen. I assume the team that signs him will give him a chance to start next year. If he winds up in relief, Taira has the stuff and gumption to get high-leverage outs in the late innings.

body:
I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks. I went 14-1 straight-up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place. 
There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell. 
If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games. The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out. 
Actually, before we get to the Week 10 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here. Also, I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com and if you want me invading your inbox twice a week, then you should definitely sign up. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address. If you do that, it will instantly make us best friends and you don't even have to feel bad about that because I've already let all my best friends know that they might be replaced this week. Alright, now let's get to the picks for realNFL Week 10 picksCommanders (2-5-1) at Giants (5-2-1)Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET (Amazon Prime)Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders, I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation. For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants. Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did. 
Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost. Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams, they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works. 
Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called. In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds. 
So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team. To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders. PICK: Commanders 24-17 over GiantsPatriots (5-4) vs. Lions (6-2) in MunichSunday, 9:30 a.m. (NFL Network)With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell?
With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first. I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me. 
The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes. 
The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever. All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year. The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams. 
The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to 9 touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over. PICK: Lions 34-27 over PatriotsTexans (3-5) at Browns (Browns 5-4)Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox)Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns, but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge on him or he's trying to get revenge on the Texans. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, there might not be any revenge involved at all here. Since trading Watson to the Browns in March 2022, the Texans have made the playoffs three times, and they've won their division twice. On the other hand, Watson has been injured for the majority of his time in Cleveland; he's won just 14 games since 2022, and the Browns have paid him roughly $14.5 million per win. If Tom Brady had earned $14.5 million per win, he would have made over $3 billion in his career. Do you know how many Hofbrauhaus beers you could buy with that money?
The worst part for the Browns is that they're still in QB purgatory, which is basically where they've been since returning to the NFL in 1999. Although Watson is playing well this year, especially late in games, I'm not sure that's a good thing. If he somehow leads Cleveland to the playoffs, the Browns might actually talk themselves into re-signing him, which doesn't seem like a great idea. Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Watson might get sacked 10 times in this game. PICK: Texans 24-16 over BrownsVikings (6-2) at Packers (6-3)Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox)When I look back at the scores from Week 1, the most shocking result might have been the Vikings' 39-22 win over the Packers. One reason it was shocking is that I'm not even sure the Vikings have scored 39 points since that game. The other reason it was shocking is that the Packers became the first team in 12 years to lose by at least 17 in a game where they held a double-digit lead in the second half. 
If there are two things I'm convinced about in this game, it's that the Vikings are NOT going to score 39 points (or even half that number) and the Packers are not going to blow a double-digit lead (and that's mainly because I don't think they'll have a double-digit lead). This matchup will be giving us strength vs. strength: The Vikings have the NFL's top passing defense and they're going to have to figure out how to slow down Jordan Love, who leads the NFC in passing yards per game (290.9). Love is on quite on the hot streak right now: He's thrown for at least 270 yards in five straight games, which is something that not even Brett Favre ever accomplished. That's right, the young gunslinger is out-slinging the Ol' gunslinger. Love has been hot because he has two receivers he completely trusts: Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. Those two BOTH went over 150 yards in Week 9 and they both had a touchdown. Do you know how many Packers' receiving duos have hit those numbers in the same game over the past 80 years? ZERO. Golden and Watson were the first ones. 
One downside for the Packers in this game is that they won't have Josh Jacobs, but that might not actually be a downside, since they didn't have him in Week 1 and Love still threw for nearly 400 yards. The Vikings started 6-0, but they're now in the reality check portion of their schedule: They're coming off back-to-back losses (Lions, Bills) and with the Packers and 49ers coming up, that losing streak could be at four in a row before Thanksgiving. PICK: Packers 20-17 over VikingsSteelers (6-2) at Bengals (6-2)Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC)After spending nearly an entire week in Spain, the Bengals are back in the United States, and this time, they have to face their toughest opponent of the year: The NFL scheduling department. For Sunday, the NFL scheduling department has put the Bengals in a situation where no team has ever won. The Bengals will enter Week 10 after playing in Madrid, and they face a Steelers team coming off a bye. This will mark just the sixth time in NFL history that a team coming off an international game has had to play a team coming off a bye, and uh, I have some bad news for everyone in Cincinnati: The team coming off the international game has gone 0-5 (and 0-4-1 against the spread). Also, NFL teams are a combined 13-1 coming off their bye this year. And just when you thought it couldn't get any worse for the Bengals, I have more bad news: The team coming off the international trip has averaged just 15 points per game, and the ugly part is that they've been outscored 83-37 over the first three quarters in those five games. I feel like the Bengals should file a protest with Roger Goodell. I'm not sure that would actually do anything, but maybe it would guilt the NFL into never doing this to another team ever again. Oh wait, it's too late for that because the Lions will be in the same situation next week. The problem with this situation is that the team returning from Europe usually needs a brief adjustment period. The jet lag after the flight back to the United States usually lasts a day or two, which means it can impact practice for your next game.These two teams met back in Week 3 and the Steelers won because they exploited two weaknesses in the Bengals defense: Cincinnati struggles to stop the run (Jaylen Warren went off for 127 yards) and the Bengals struggle to cover tight ends (Steelers tight ends combined to make five catches for 97 yards). Overall, the Steelers offense simply played its best game of the season. They finished with 411 yards. They have not topped 365 in any other game.I have a hard time seeing that happen again. If anyone can end this 0-5 international curse, it's Joe Burrow. He's playing quarterback at a higher level than anyone right now, and he's going to be out for revenge. Not only are the Bengals playing at home in primetime, but they're wearing their white tiger helmets, and I'm not picking against the white tiger helmets. PICK: Bengals 27-24 over SteelersNFL 10 picks: All the restChiefs 27-20 over FalconsJaguars 31-16 over TitansColts 19-16 over DolphinsPanthers 23-20 over SaintsBills 30-20 over JetsSeahawks 27-17 over RaidersRams 23-16 over Cardinals49ers 31-24 over CowboysRavens 20-16 over ChargersLast WeekBest pick: Bengals over Falcons. Last week, I predicted that the Bengals would score exactly 34 points and win the game in Spain and guess what happened? The Bengals scored exactly 34 points and won the game in Spain. When the Bengals left for Madrid last week, Joe Burrow wore a Pikachu hoodie on the flight over, and there's no way you're letting yourself be photographed in a Pikachu hoodie unless you're 100% sure that your team is going to win. As soon as I saw that photo, I was 100% sure the Bengals were going to win. 
The twist here is that Pikachu isn't even Burrow's favorite Pokémon, and the only reason I know that is that someone actually asked him that exact question on Sunday. 
That's why we need more games played abroad. The international reporters aren't afraid to ask the hard-hitting questions. Worst pick: Browns over Saints. I only missed one pick last week -- THIS ONE -- so I have to put this game here even though I don't even think it was a bad pick. There were at least five different occasions where I thought the Browns were going to win this, but this is the Browns we're talking about, so they eventually found a way to blow it. The one thing I didn't take into account is that the Browns' defense seems to be getting worse every week. 
At the rate things are going, the Browns are going to give up 700 yards to the Colts in Week 17. Finally, if you guys have ever wondered which teams I'm actually good at picking, I'm going to start sharing that information every week from now through the end of the season. Here's a quick look at my best and worst teams when it comes to picks this year. Team: I'm 8-1 picking this year (Straight up): Patriots, Eagles, Jaguars (7-1), Dolphins (7-1), Commanders (6-1-1)My worst teams this year (Straight up): Bears (3-6), Buccaneers (3-6), Browns (3-6)Every other team is somewhere in the middle. Picks recordStraight up in Week 9: 14-1SU overall: 82-53-1Against the spread in Week 9: 11-4ATS overall: 63-70-3BREECHIGAMIS: 1You can find John Breech on Facebook, TikTok or Twitter, and if he's not doing one of those things, he's probably trying to round up some friends to see if they want to tailgate at the Taco Bell by his house this weekend.

description: A look at the top-performing freshmen in college basketball last week and for the 2026-27 season
body:
A look at the top-performing freshmen in college basketball last week and for the 2026-27 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:59 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        What if I told you the freshman who had the best performance during the opening week of the 2026-27 college basketball season isn't even eligible for the 2027 NBA Draft? Yes, you read that right. In an era of one-and-dones, UCLA's Nikola Kusturica will be the rare player in the sport who plays at least two seasons before entering the draft.Of course, that's not necessarily by choice. If Kusturica were eligible for this summer's draft, he would have a very strong case to go No. 1. Kusturica, Duke freshman Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje and Texas' Marcus Spears Jr. won't turn 18 until 2027, meaning they don't meet the draft's age requirement to be eligible for this summer's draft.It's great news for college basketball fans, but bad news for NBA teams looking to add a foundational piece to their rosters. Last season featured arguably the greatest freshman class in college basketball history, with AJ Dybantsa, Cameron Boozer, Caleb Wilson, Darius Acuff Jr., Darryn Peterson, and many more making their mark on the sport.
        
            
                Why Duke's Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje, UCLA's Nikola Kusturica, Texas' Marcus Spears can't enter 2027 NBA Draft
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
This year's class certainly has talent, but expectations should be tempered after last year's greatness. However, after two impressive performances against Arizona and North Florida, Kusturica showed this week why he could be considered the best prospect in the world, regardless of draft class
Let's jump into our rankings and get to our CBS Sports/USBWA Freshman of the Week for the 2026-27 college basketball season.Freshman of the Week: Nikola Kusturica, UCLAWelcome back to the Frosh Watch, our weekly ranking of the five most impressive freshmen in college basketball. For the 12th season in a row, CBS Sports has once again teamed up with the United States Basketball Writers Association and its Wayman Tisdale Freshman of the Year Award to present this every-Tuesday feature. Each week, we'll start by announcing the national Freshman of the Week honoree. The cycle for FOTW runs Tuesday-Monday.After Kusturica finished with 29 points, six rebounds, three assists and two blocks in a blowout win over North Florida, UCLA coach Mick Cronin had high praise for his star 17-year-old forward.
"He's a great player," Cronin said. "Not a good player, a great player because he does everything on the court. What I would tell you is he had no turnovers with the ball in his hands all the time, which for a freshman, is unheard of."
What's even more impressive about that stat line is that he recorded zero turnovers against North Florida and Arizona. Even when he's not scoring, Kusturica can impact the game. He finished with three blocks and two steals during UCLA's upset win over Arizona on opening night. UCLA hasn't had a draft prospect of his caliber since Lozno Ball nearly a decade ago.Frosh Watch: Ranking top five freshmen
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Nikola Kusturica | F | UCLAStats: 19.0 PPG | 5.5 RPG | 2.5 APG Kusturica looks extremely comfortable playing college basketball despite being just 17 years old. He's already proven he can make an impact without scoring, but can also put together efficient and productive offensive performances. In UCLA's win over North Florida, Kusturica hit his first nine shots and finished with 29 points in just 26 minutes of action. He went 10-for-12 from the field, 4-for-5 from three, and 5-for-5 from the free-throw line. He added six rebounds, three assists, and two blocks. There's a reason why there's significant buzz about Kusturica going No. 1 overall in the 2028 NBA Draft. He already looks like a star.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Tyran Stokes | F | KansasStats: 11.5 PPG | 6.0 RPG | 1.5 APG Stokes, the projected No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA Draft, began his college career with 15 points, seven rebounds and a block during a blowout win over Fordham. Stokes has played only 46 minutes in his first two games because both games were blowouts. He will get expanded opportunity when Kansas faces Kentucky in the Champions Classic on Tuesday.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Miles Sadler | G | West VirginiaStats: 20.5 PPG | 2.5 RPG | 7.5 APG Sadler is already one of the most exciting players to watch in college basketball. The 6-foot guard was a preseason Freshman All-American by CBS Sports. The first two games of his college career were why he earned that honor. Sadler scored 25 points in his second college game during a win over Stetson. He also has 15 total assists across his first two games. WVU will go as far as Sadler takes them.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Quentin Coleman | G | IllinoisStats: 16.0 PPG | 6.5 RPG | 4.0 APG Last year, it was Keaton Wagler who stole the show and went from unsung recruit to star. While Coleman was a more highly touted prospect coming out of high school, he already looks like a very serious impact player for one of the best teams in the country. Coleman nearly recorded a triple-double (13 points, 10 rebounds and six assists) in just 23 minutes in his college debut. He followed that up by scoring 19 points in just 20 minutes per game. Illinois will once again have one of the best offenses in the country.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Jordan Smith Jr. | G | ArkansasStats: 19.5 PPG | 3.5 RPG | 2.0 APG Smith finished with 19 points, four steals and three assists during a loss to Virginia last weekend. In his college debut, he scored 20 points and recorded three steals. Smith is a very impactful two-way player who looks like the next great John Calipari-coached guard.

        This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
🤯 Five things to know Tuesday Josh Allen and the Bills outlasted a listless Vikings offense. The quarterback matchup between Josh Allen and Carson Wentz went exactly as you'd expect. Minnesota wasted an excellent defensive performance with an atrocious effort on offense in a 23-6 loss. On the other side, Allen and the Bills deserve high marks for sticking with it despite starting slow against one of the NFL's best defenses.Rams star Puka Nacua will land on IR. The hits just keep coming for a Rams team that entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations. The latest blow came in the form of knee and toe injuries to Nacua, who will miss at least the next four games on IR.         Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Reds were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year in their respective leagues on Monday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. McGonigle earned 28 of 30 first-place votes, beating out the Guardians' Parker Messick and the Red Sox's Payton Tolle. Stewart, meanwhile, beat the Mets' Carson Benge and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt.Because McGonigle and Stewart were both with the major-league team for long enough to earn a full year of service time, the Tigers and Reds will each receive a Prospect Promotion Incentive pick in the 2027 MLB Draft. The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    National League: Sal Stewart, RedsStewart won the battle of Old School stats vs. New School stats here. Though he only posted 2.0 WAR, he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The only names from that list to not win the award either faced another player from the list or played before Rookie of the Year was awarded. Everyone else has taken home the hardware, just as Stewart did Monday evening.
Overall, Stewart appeared in all 162 games, hitting .263/.330/.457 (117 OPS+) with 25 doubles, 32 homers, 112 RBI, 87 runs and 15 steals. Stewart earned 20 of the 30 available first-place votes.Player1st2nd3rd4th5thPointsSal Stewart, Reds205131170Carson Benge, Mets731242107JJ Wetherholt, Cardinals31265299Nolan McLean, Mets679770TJ Rumfield, Rockies3391049Logan Henderson, Brewers11310Bryce Eldridge, Brewers22Didier Fuentes, Braves22A.J. Ewing, Mets11Carson Benge of the Mets finished second and JJ Wetherholt of the Cardinals finished in third place. Benge, the 2024 first-rounder, made the team out of spring training and hit .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and 4.3 WAR. Defensive metrics love Wetherholt and helped push him to 4.5 WAR in 139 games. He hit .242/.339/.365 with 17 homers, 14 steals and 89 runs.Stewart joins the following Reds as Rookie of the Year winners: Jonathan India, 2021Scott Williamson, 1999Chris Sabo, 1988Pat Zachry, 1976Johnny Bench, 1968Tommy Helms, 1966Pete Rose, 1963Frank Robinson, 1956
                            
    
                                                
                    
    American League: Kevin McGonigle, TigersThe honor for McGonigle completes a stellar year for the former first-round draft pick. He broke camp with the Tigers and was productive from the get-go. He ended up hitting .278/.376/.430 (126 OPS+) with 28 doubles, five triples, 18 home runs, 72 RBI, 97 runs, 12 steals and 7.1 WAR, the latter good enough for the AL lead among position players. He played great defense, ran the bases well and was an All-Star. He nearly walked (95) as much as he struck out (100), too. Not much more could've been asked of the Pennsylvania native who played most of the season at age 21, and he's a well-deserving Rookie of the Year.

title: Six lessons learned from NFL Week 9: Arvell Reese a superstar in the making, C.J. Stroud having career year - CBS Sports
description: Plus, there's a bell cow running back emerging for one of the NFL's best teams
body:
Plus, there's a bell cow running back emerging for one of the NFL's best teams
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the trade deadline today, I am reminded that self-awareness is of one of the best attributes an organization can have, from top to bottom.The team that comes to mind immediately is one we've heard a lot from -- not in a good way -- this year: the Colts. Around this time last year, Indianapolis sent away two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner in a trade-deadline blockbuster. Indianapolis was 7-2 at the time, but was it really a team that needed to go all-in? No. Daniel Jones was playing so over-his-head well, and a smart front office would have recognized the great record was a product of a very soft schedule, a little bit of luck and an unprecedented hot streak. There was no rush here. The 2025 season was supposed to be a transition one, and a medium-sized cornerback addition would have been fine. Again, just a few months earlier, Indianapolis was basically taking a flyer on Jones.You know how the rest of the story goes. Jones and the offense start to fall off, then Jones ruptures his Achilles. Now, the Colts are 2-7 and in the midst of a franchise-altering sale while not even owning their first-round pick. If the draft started today, Indianapolis would send the No. 4 pick to the Jets. Yikes!The Jets, meanwhile, continue to profit in a big way off of that trade and the Quinnen Williams trade. They currently own the No. 4 (Colts'), No. 6 (their own) and No. 13 (Cowboys') picks. They knew this would be a long process. They knew it could be ugly for a while, and this year's 2-7 mark confirms that. But New York could have a terrific kickstart to their rebuild in a few months' time.
One team fell for fool's gold. The other knew exactly where it was and embraced its unenviable role.The Jets are still waiting to fully invest in their rebuild. The other New York team? Well, it has already started -- and is way ahead of schedule -- thanks to a different type of self-awareness.1. Arvell Reese is a superstar in the makingPlease just watch these highlights first, then pick your jaw up from off the floor and continue reading below.
Some fun stats for you:Reese is the youngest player with a three-sack game since the stat became official for individuals in 1982 Reese is the only player in the NFL with 65 tackles, eight tackles for loss and an interception this season.Reese is the first rookie to hit all three of those milestones within his team's first eight games since Luke Kuechly in 2012.The biggest question surrounding Reese during the build-up to the NFL Draft was "Where do you play him?"The answer should have been another question: "Why does it matter?"And the Giants were exactly right to take that approach. Reese was an EDGE at Ohio State who moonlighted at off-ball linebacker. When the Giants initially drafted him, John Harbaugh basically said he'd play linebacker but also move around. Through eight games, Reese has now played at least 30 snaps at seven different spots: right inside linebacker, left inside linebacker, right linebacker, right EDGE, left linebacker, middle linebacker and left EDGE.This is the way the NFL is trending. Think about guys such as Seattle's Nick Emmanwori, technically a safety who really plays everywhere, and someone we've talked about in this column before. Reese is of that ilk: a truly, laughably absurd athlete. A weapon who transcends positional labels. His strip sack of Joe Milton happened in 2.29 seconds, the fastest sack of the year per Next Gen Stats.
Here's where the self-awareness portion comes in. The Giants knew neither they nor Reese had to have it figured out on Day 1. The Giants are in Year 1 under John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Reese is 21 years old. The world was (and still is!) their oyster to experiment. Reese looks phenomenal. The Giants are 5-2-1 despite having started three different quarterbacks, and players such as Reese give them a bright future, too.2. C.J. Stroud is the best quarterback you're not paying attention toI do not blame you if you didn't watch -- or even think twice (or once) -- about the Texans-Chargers Week 9 matchup. The Chargers are unwatchable, and the Texans are middling after coming into the season with Super Bowl expectations.What you missed and may have missed for much of this season, though, is C.J. Stroud playing outstanding football. He threw five touchdown passes Sunday, and his highlights ranged from heart-warming ...
(Welcome back, Tank Dell!)... to jaw-dropping.
Lest you think "Oh, it's just the Chargers," they've actually been decent on defense this year. This was just Stroud putting on a clinic. It's been this way all year.C.J. Stroud this yearNFL rankCareer-best?TD-Int16-22ndYesPassing success rate48.7%11thYesNegative play rate6.9%6thYesEPA per dropback0.186thYesThe Texans' 3-5 record is mostly due to a surprisingly up-and-down defense and major struggles on the ground. DeMeco Ryans hasn't been great situationally, either. Even if Houston doesn't make the playoffs, Stroud's play is huge for Stroud himself -- he entered the year without an extension on his rookie deal -- and for Houston, which can feel much better about handing Stroud said extension.On a week in which Jordan Love and Joe Burrow stole the spotlight, don't forget about Stroud.3. The Vikings need to trade for a quarterbackDid you watch Monday night?I could leave it there, but I won't. Carson Wentz isn't the answer -- clearly. Kyler Murray has never looked comfortable in this offense. Is Geno Smith the answer? A reunion with Kirk Cousins? It can't be worse than it's been, and Minnesota simply cannot waste this defense again.4. Jonah Coleman taking over the Broncos' backfield is a good thing for DenverJonah Coleman recorded 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers. He played 53 of Denver's 65 snaps, second-most of any skill-position player behind Courtland Sutton. He also played nine of Denver's 10 third-down snaps.J.K. Dobbins, on the other hand, played just nine snaps overall, and zero on third down. After some injuries earlier this year, Coleman owns this backfield -- especially until RJ Harvey returns -- and that's a good thing.Broncos RBs this seasonColemanDobbinsHarveyYards per rush4.13.63.3Explosive run rate9%5%0%Yards per rush vs. 8-man box5.41.61.0Pct of runs with missed tackle forced17%14%4%Coleman already has as many rushing touchdowns (three) as Dobbins has despite having less than half of Dobbins' carries.
Let's remember that Coleman is a fourth-round rookie, too. He should continue to get better. Denver's reportedly been shopping around for running backs, but if it doesn't land one, Coleman will emerge as an early-down bell cow (with Harvey more in the mix on late downs) down the stretch.Just, please, Sean Payton, no more pitch plays in late-game, wind-the-clock scenarios. I think Bo Nix agrees.5. Evan Williams is a starWe highlighted Evan Williams a few weeks ago, but that was really more about Jonathan Gannon. After a game that included an incredible interception, four pressures and five tackles, Williams gets his own slot here.The four pressures were a season high for Williams, who blitzed a season-high eight times. On one blitz, he basically shoulder-checked Rhamondre Stevenson (a good pass-blocking back) to the side and forced a throwaway. On another, he didn't get near Drake Maye but tracked back and limited Maye's scramble to 3 yards. On his final blitz of the day, he ran right by Lan Larison and nearly got a strip sack.Williams is a combination of a high-speed train and a bumper car attacking the quarterback. If you don't try to stop him, he'll chase you down, and when you do try to stop him, he bounces off and keeps going. He now has a ridiculous 38.2% pressure rate on 34 pass-rush snaps this season.Oh yeah, and did we mention he can do this on the back end?
And this?
Now for the numbers:Williams is PFF's No. 1-graded safety this year: first in coverage and sixth in rush defense.He makes a tackle on 15.5% of his snaps against the run, the fifth-highest rate among 84 defensive backs with at least 400 snaps entering "Monday Night Football."Individual coverage tracking can be iffy, but Williams is allowing 3.8 yards per attempt as the primary defender, 10th out of 195 players who had been targeted at least 20 times entering "Monday Night Football."His passer rating allowed -- 36.2 -- is even better: fourth out that same 195-player sample. For reference, throwing the ball incomplete every play would result in a 39.6 passer rating.Good player. Really, really good player. All-Pro player.6. The NFC South is approaching all-time bad territoryIt was a rough week for the NFC South. The Falcons got shellacked by the Bengals in Madrid, the Panthers lost at home to the Broncos, and the Buccaneers wasted five Bears turnovers in a loss in Chicago. The division's lone winner -- the Saints -- got an uninspiring 23-22 overtime win over Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. A failed two-point conversion is all that stood between the NFC South and an 0-4 week.The 2026 NFC South is the only division ever with every team at least two games below .500 through Week 9. The Panthers and the Saints are 3-5, and the Buccaneers and the Falcons are 3-6. The combined 12-22 record is on pace to be the third-worst by any division since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.SportsLine currently does not project any NFC South team to reach eight wins. There's never been a seven-win playoff team in the 17-game era (since 2021).But SportsLine projections also has every team reaching at least six wins, setting up for some major late-season drama. Remember last year, when the Buccaneers beat the Panthers to take the NFC South lead in Week 18, only for Carolina to win the division thanks to a tiebreaker because the Falcons beat the Saints the next day? Yeah, prepare for some weirdness.

title: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew feared to have suffered a torn UCL, could be out for season, per report - CBS Sports
description: Carson Beck would get the start if Minshew is sidelined
body:
Carson Beck would get the start if Minshew is sidelined
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals offensive injuries continue to pile up. Shortly after head coach Mike LaFleur announced wide receiver Michael Wilson would be ruled out for the year with a neck injury and added there was a chance Gardner Minshew misses Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams, reports came out that the quarterback is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.According to NFL Network, Minshew could be out for the season and face "months of rehab," pending further testing. Minshew reportedly suffered the injury before halftime but played through it in last week's 17-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks. If Minshew is sidelined, Carson Beck would be the next man up. Beck would be the third quarterback to start for the Cardinals this season. Jacoby Brissett began the year as their starter before being benched and traded to the Baltimore Ravens earlier this month. Since Beck would be the team's only QB on the depth chart if Minshew is out for the year, team reportedly acted fast to get some backup. On Monday, the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad, according to ESPN. This marks Johnson's 15th NFL team in 14 seasons.Beck was drafted in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 65 overall. The two-time College Football Playoff national champion has yet to make an appearance in the NFL. He would be the third rookie quarterback to start a game this season, joining Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels and Washington Commanders seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis. 
The 24-year-old spent five years at Georgia and his last collegiate season with Miami (FL). He finished with 338 completions, a conference high, for 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. His 72.4 completion percentage was also a conference high.In 55 total college games, he had 966 completions for 11,725 yards, 88 touchdowns and 32 interceptions. After Brissett's eight games, the team made a change at QB during the third quarter of their Nov. 1 game against the Cowboys, putting in Minshew. Beck was promoted to backup quarterback, with Brissett demoted to the third-string QB shortly before his exit from Arizona.Minshew played two games, with a 71.7 completion percentage, 354 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, going 0-1 in starts.
The Cardinals currently sit at 3-6 and are in fourth place in the NFC West.

title: Fantasy Football: Puka Nacua injury replacements, trade targets and waiver adds - CBS Sports
description: Puka Nacua's injury leaves a massive Fantasy void, but these trade targets and waiver-wire options could help sav
body:
Puka Nacua's injury leaves a massive Fantasy void, but these trade targets and waiver-wire options could help save your season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As soon as Myles Garrett came back and made a huge impact for the Rams on defense, the Rams offense lost one of its impact players when head coach Sean McVay announced Puka Nacua will "be out a good amount of time" with an MCL/PCL sprain and turf toe.For the Rams, and for Fantasy Football managers, there is no replacing Nacua. He's averaged 13.3 targets, 10 catches, 102.1 receiving yards and 24.8 PPR points per game. The man is a unicorn.  Trying to guess the Rams' next move is dangerous. When Nacua went down with an injury in Week 1 of the 2024 season, everyone assumed Tutu Atwell, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Whittington would all take on more work. They did, but none averaged more than the 11.4 PPR points Atwell reeled in over five games (he also averaged 6.8 targets per game). That includes tight end Colby Parkinson, by the way.  Moreover, in those games, the Rams went 2-3, averaged 18.8 points per game and ran the ball 44% of their plays.  
Their offense simply was not the same without Nacua. And it won't be the same this time around, either. Not until Davante Adams comes back, but that figures to be by Week 12 at the earliest. And tight end Terrance Ferguson will be "another couple of weeks" out, according to McVay, who said before Week 9 that he hurt his hamstring in practice.What should Fantasy managers do?Don't look to the Rams depth chart to find a winning solution at receiver. Look to other receivers around the league. Remember, the goal here is to simply find a receiver who you can start with some confidence -- a guy who can average six targets per week, preferably with a good quarterback on a team that throws a lot, would be a good enough Band-Aid. Receivers to trade forCarnell Tate, Titans: He should be healthy coming out of the bye, and he's seen at least six targets in four of his past five. His schedule is mostly good; Cam Ward has made some slow progress in his game, and the Titans probably won't have many low-pass-volume game scripts. He also shouldn't cost too much in trade. Tate is the receiver on this list I'd chase the most.  
Jalen Coker, Panthers: Coker has been on a dry spell, much like the Panthers, but he obviously plays a lot and works as a short-area outlet for Bryce Young. His target volume has sunk in his past three games and the Panthers offensively are finding ways to stay competitive despite a depleted offensive line. His schedule is mostly great — until Weeks 15 through 17. Maybe the most appealing part of acquiring Coker is the very low cost it'll take to get him given his recent weak stats.  Jordyn Tyson, Saints: The rookie had a sensational 31.3% target-per-route run rate in his debut last week, lining up in the slot just as much as he did out wide. He definitely flashed quicks out of his breaks and the same kind of acceleration we saw in college. The Saints haven't found a reliable run game all year, and because their remaining schedule isn't too daunting, we should see them throw a lot. That should mean Tyson winds up second on the team in targets from this point forward.  Denzel Boston, Browns: Cleveland's best threat outside the numbers, Boston has gotten at least seven targets in five of his past six, and he has nine red-zone targets on the year. Unfortunately, Boston's been above 10 PPR points in just three of those six. He does see an 83.6% catchable target rate, the fourth-lowest compared to 22 other players with at least 60 targets, so his quarterback play does keep his ceiling low. But the Browns' run game is a mess and their schedule after the Week 11 bye is amazing.   
KC Concepcion, Browns: Like Boston, Concepcion gets a lot of targets, but unlike Boston, they're all mostly short-area screens and slants. That leads to easier completions (his catchable target rate is slightly better at 85.5%), but his floor is lower. Then again, if the Browns schedule is good for the pass game after Week 11, then Concepcion should be able to break a bunch of big plays after the catch. That'll be his only pathway to huge numbers, since he has a grand total of two red-zone targets in 2026.  If you can get them cheap ... Nico Collins and Garrett Wilson are also good receivers to target, but the people who roster them might be a little delusional in what they'd want in return. If you're willing to pay a pretty penny, then go after one of those two before the cheaper thrills listed above.  Receivers to add off waiversTank Dell, Texans (22% rostered): The dude had nine targets despite a 55% route rate in a blowout win over the Chargers. Seven of the nine targets were deep shots, of which he caught two. There's no doubt that C.J. Stroud loves having him back on the field, and the Texans' run game has been a wreck all year. Therefore, the Texans' chase for a playoff spot will go through Stroud's arm.  
Makai Lemon, Eagles (59% rostered): You'll have to deal with his Week 10 bye, but the Eagles are heading toward a lost season with a depleted defense, making it more likely that the offense will throw a lot. Even with DeVonta Smith coming back at some point, Lemon should still be in the six-target range.  Caleb Douglas, Dolphins (73% rostered on CBS; lower on other platforms): It's beginning to look like Douglas will work as Miami's No. 1 receiver moving forward. He's got very good size and good speed to go with it, and the Dolphins offense will probably lean pass-heavy. Maybe four tough matchups are in front of him, but he should be another youngster worth your time.  Adonai Mitchell, Jets (63% rostered): His seven-target, zero-catch outing against the Chiefs might deter you, but Geno Smith has been completely willing to keep firing at Mitchell. And let's be fair, a week ago he had 142 yards and a touchdown. His schedule gets prickly once you get near the Fantasy playoffs.  
Tutu Atwell, Rams (1% rostered): When the Rams were without Nacua for five games in 2024, Atwell stepped in and was the only pass-catcher to notch more than two weeks with double-digit PPR points. I'd be surprised if Atwell was just as good this time around, but he's a known quantity to this coaching staff -- they signed him to a crazy one-year deal last year, barely used him, then let him go in free agency to the Dolphins before trading for him before the season started!   If you don't mind streaming ... Ryan Flournoy (59% rostered), Demario Douglas (82% rostered on CBS; lower on other platforms), Jordan Watkins (25% rostered), Mack Hollins (12% rostered) and Xavier Hutchinson (6% rostered) are all worth taking a peek at. Hutchinson, like Dell, should play a lot in the slot for the Texans' pass-heavy offense.
